title: refactor(ci): unify lint/test/release workflows, bump GH Actions and deps, optimize cache parallelism
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Consolidate CI workflows into unified lint/test/release pipelines; upgrade GitHub Actions and workflow runner images; optimize cache keys and parallelism to reduce build time and flakiness.
description: Motivation: CI has drifted over time with duplicated workflow logic, multiple runner images, and inconsistent cache keys leading to slower pipelines and intermittent flakes. This PR consolidates lint, test, and release workflows into a unified, composable set of workflows, bumps key GitHub Actions and runner images to recommended versions, and optimizes cache key generation and job parallelism. Goals: 1) Reduce CI maintenance surface by centralizing reusable steps and templates, 2) Improve build performance by reducing redundant jobs and improving cache hit rates, 3) Reduce flakes by standardizing runner images and test matrices. What changed: unified workflows under .github/workflows (lint.yml, test.yml, release.yml) with reusable workflow_call templates, extracted common steps into .github/actions and .github/workflows/templates, bumped actions/setup-node to v3 and actions/cache to v4, replaced ubuntu-18/20 runner references with ubuntu-22, consolidated matrix configs to reduce redundant builds, and introduced a stable cache key hashing script to avoid duplicate caches across similar matrices. Checklist: - [x] Consolidate workflows and templates - [x] Bump GH Actions and runner images - [x] Verify cache keys and parallelism settings - [x] Run full CI across redwood monorepo - [x] Address reviewer feedback and flakiness found in unit-tests How to review: focus on workflow templates and cache-key logic; changes to application code are limited to CI helpers and package.json devDependency bumps. Related: ENG-4231 tracks the umbrella CI refactor; SUP-9821 surfaced a production incident caused by delayed release automation due to a stale token workflow. This PR is intended to be non-breaking for product code and to improve CI reliability and speed.
